sentences.en: Well, I want you to say more about that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你，我们总是在寻找，我想，对吧，我是一个记者，我是一个退伍军人。

sentences.en: I mean, what did it mean to you, particularly as a former Marine who served in this war, to see a base in this, as you said, post-apocalyptic
sentences.zh: 就像我们总是在寻找，尤其是在这一切结束的现在，你某种程度上在寻找那些能够宣告这一切就是

sentences.en: state, just kind of frozen in place, no longer occupied by your fellow soldiers?
sentences.zh: 终点的时刻，你知道，就像一场瞻仰遗容的葬礼一样，来做个告别。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想那个食堂绝对会被记入那些记忆之中。

sentences.en: I mean, it, it, it, it, it was, it was an outer body experience, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想让你多谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: Experiencing something that is so simple, like a saran wrapped serving station, an empty defect menu, a clock
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对你来说，特别是作为一个曾在这次战争中服役的前海军陆战队员，看到一个基地处于你所说的这种末日废土

sentences.en: on the wall, and knowing that you're experiencing something that you'll have to process for a long time.
sentences.zh: 般的状态，就那样定格在原地，不再由你的战友们占领，这意味着什么？

sentences.en: I mean, that's kind of Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's, it's the hotel, California.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它，它，它，它真是一种灵魂出窍般的体验，对吧？

sentences.en: You can check out, but you can't ever leave.
sentences.zh: 体验一些如此简单的事情，比如用保鲜膜包裹的配餐台、一份空的食堂菜单、墙上的时钟

sentences.en: You know, you go through these very chaotic moments, I guess, in my early twenties.
sentences.zh: ，并且知道你正在经历一件需要你花很长时间去消化的事情。

sentences.en: And then to link that to the present, you know, is important, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是阿富汗。

sentences.en: Like this is what the end looks like.
sentences.zh: 它就是加州旅馆。

sentences.en: You remember the middle and maybe the beginning.
sentences.zh: 你可以退房，但你永远无法离开。

sentences.en: But now you have this moment where you can kind of close it out so selfishly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在二十出头的时候经历过这些非常混乱的时刻，然后将那段经历与现在联系起来，你知道，这很重要，对吧？这就是结局的样子。你还记得中间的过程，也许还有开始。但现在你有了这样一个时刻，你可以用这种自私的方式为它画上句号。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I think it was really important for me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这对我来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: Tim, you said earlier that the Afghans now control these bases.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆，你之前说过阿富汗人现在控制着这些基地。

sentences.en: And I wonder what that handover looks like and what now happens to these bases.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这种交接是怎样的，这些基地现在又会怎样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, the, the handover of these bases has been kind of a mystery, you know, for some of the larger bases, they were handed over in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些基地的交接有点像个谜，你知道的，对于一些较大的基地，它们是在半夜交接的。

sentences.en: And it seems with a lack of complete coordination with the, with the Afghan security forces, the American military would push
sentences.zh: 而且似乎缺乏与阿富汗安全部队的完全协调，美军会反驳

sentences.en: back and say, this has been extremely well-coordinated.
sentences.zh: 并说这已经得到了极其良好的协调。

sentences.en: But at the heart of it, the Americans and, you know, quote unquote, operational security concerns seemed inclined to not give the Afghan security forces
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，美国人和，你知道的，所谓的作战安全关切似乎倾向于不告诉阿富汗安全部队

sentences.en: their exact time of departure, because there's a fear of, you know, some kind of attack or insider
sentences.zh: 他们确切的离开时间，因为人们担心，你知道的，某种袭击或内部

sentences.en: attack or someone in the security forces might leak something to the Taliban or a disgruntled soldier,
sentences.zh: 袭击，或者安全部队中的某个人可能会向塔利班泄露消息，或者一个心怀不满的士兵，

sentences.en: Afghan soldier would fire on, on the Americans.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗士兵会向美国人开枪。

sentences.en: So I think it's, it's played out a little
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，就这一点而言，

sentences.en: disjointedly, uh, as far as that's concerned.
sentences.zh: 事情的进展有点脱节。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it sounds like these transfers are happening with no ceremony and no fanfare and some level of distrust for the people who are taking it over.
sentences.zh: 听起来这些转移没有任何仪式、没有盛大的场面，而且对接管的人有着一定程度的不信任。

sentences.en: And I have to say, although this was personally powerful for you to see as a veteran of the war, it all feels very anticlimactic.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，尽管作为战争老兵，你亲眼看到这一切很有感触，但这一切都让人觉得非常虎头蛇尾。

sentences.en: The end of these bases after a 20 year war, after all the blood and treasure that was devoted to it, to have such a rushed, disjointed, as you said,
sentences.zh: 在经历了20年的战争、付出了所有的鲜血和财富之后，这些基地的终结，竟然是以你所说的这种仓促、脱节的、

sentences.en: middle of the night handover of these bases from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 半夜三更的方式将这些基地从美军手中

sentences.en: to the Afghan forces.
sentences.zh: 移交给阿富汗军队。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And anticlimactic is, is the word to use.
sentences.zh: 而“虎头蛇尾”就是用来形容这种情况的词。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact that this is kind of just
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上这一切就这么

sentences.en: quietly happening and the press has to kind of rush and find out that it happened to, to write their story or, you know, to use it as a mile marker or a monument to, to the war.
sentences.zh: 悄悄地发生了，媒体不得不赶忙去弄清楚它已经发生，来写他们的报道，或者，你知道的，把它当作战争的一个里程碑或纪念碑。

sentences.en: I mean, it is, is really underwhelming.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的让人觉得太不够震撼了。

sentences.en: I mean, I've, you know, seen a friend on Facebook kind of asking, well, when, when is anyone going to talk about this?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，你知道的，看到脸书上有一个朋友在问，好吧，什么时候才会有人来谈论这个？

sentences.en: When is anyone going to come out and say what this was supposed to mean?
sentences.zh: 什么时候才会有人出来说这到底意味着什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because at the end of the day, I don't think anyone in, in Washington or in the military here really knows how to answer, how does it end?
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，我认为华盛顿或这里的军方没有人真正知道该如何回答，这一切将如何结束？

sentences.en: So they just leave and one base closes after another and a press release goes out with, you know, 50% of the withdrawal is complete.
sentences.zh: 所以他们只是离开，一个基地接着一个基地关闭，然后发布新闻稿称，你知道的，50%的撤离已经完成。

sentences.en: 90% of the withdrawal is complete because no one's been able to answer that question.
sentences.zh: 90%的撤离已经完成，因为没有人能够回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone's kind of wrestling and myself included, you know, what, what that looks like or how that's supposed to feel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个人都在纠结，包括我自己在内，你知道的，这到底是什么样子的，或者这应该是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And I think the closest they've been getting is, is these closures of these bases that have kind of become monuments to the war itself,
sentences.zh: 我想他们能接近的最好的方式就是关闭这些基地，这些基地在某种程度上已经成了战争本身的纪念碑，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Because that's something you could point to.
sentences.zh: 因为那是你可以指出的东西。

sentences.en: It's something concrete.
sentences.zh: 这是具体的东西。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app unlocked.
sentences.zh: 纽约时报App已解锁。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month for free without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月而无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载纽约时报App时，你在App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》的订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅纽约时报，今天就下载时报App，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: We've been talking about the experience of these base closures for the American forces.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论美军经历的这些基地关闭的情况。

sentences.en: I wonder how this is all sitting with the Afghan people, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想知道阿富汗人民对此作何感想，美国人

sentences.en: leaving these giant installations that have become fixtures in their lives as well.
sentences.zh: 留下了这些巨大的军事设施，它们也成为了他们生活中的一部分。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's a question that I've had for some time.
sentences.zh: 这也是我一段时间以来一直在问的问题。

sentences.en: And I think one of the better examples of of that handover would be Bagram Airfield, right?
sentences.zh: 我想其中一个较好的交接例子就是巴格拉姆空军基地，对吧？

sentences.en: That was the Americans' biggest space,
sentences.zh: 那是美国人最大的基地，

sentences.en: you know, twin runway, where basically it was the anchor of the American war effort.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，拥有双跑道，基本上它是美国战争努力的支柱。

sentences.en: And I wanted to see, you know, how this base closing would affect the local communities.
sentences.zh: 我想看看，你知道的，这个基地的关闭将如何影响当地社区。

sentences.en: So last week, I went up to
sentences.zh: 所以上周，我去了

sentences.en: Bagram Air Base right before it closed.
sentences.zh: 巴格拉姆空军基地，就在它关闭前夕。

sentences.en: And I talked to people around the base to see how they felt about the closing.
sentences.zh: 我与基地周围的人交谈，看看他们对关闭有什么感受。

sentences.en: Tim, I wonder if you can describe the scene that you found outside of Bagram Air Base.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆，我想请你描述一下你在巴格拉姆空军基地外面看到的景象。

sentences.en: So to describe the scene outside of Bagram, you kind of have to understand the air base itself, right?
sentences.zh: 所以要描述巴格拉姆外面的景象，你得先了解空军基地本身，对吧？

sentences.en: And it was built in the 1950s as an airstrip that the Soviets turned into their hub for their war when they invaded in 1979.
sentences.zh: 它建于20世纪50年代，是一个简易机场，苏联人在1979年入侵时将其改造成了他们的战争枢纽。

sentences.en: And then in 2001, when the Americans arrived, it was run down kind of just the remains of a Soviet air base.
sentences.zh: 然后到了2001年美国人抵达时，它已经破败不堪，基本上只剩下苏联空军基地的残骸。

sentences.en: And throughout the years until the height of the war, I mean, the Americans built it up.
sentences.zh: 多年来直到战争最激烈的时候，我的意思是，美国人把它建了起来。

sentences.en: They built another airstrip.
sentences.zh: 他们修建了另一个简易机场。

sentences.en: There was a prison there that was extremely notorious.
sentences.zh: 那里有一座极其臭名昭著的监狱。

sentences.en: And two inmates died.
sentences.zh: 有两名囚犯死亡。

sentences.en: And by the height of the war, I mean, there were tens of thousands of people there.
sentences.zh: 到战争最激烈的时候，我的意思是，那里有几万人。

sentences.en: There were pizza huts, shopettes, post exchanges.
sentences.zh: 那里有必胜客、小型超市、邮局。

sentences.en: I mean, it was very much a city.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它非常像一个城市。

sentences.en: And as the base grew, the town around it kind of fed off it.
sentences.zh: 随着基地的发展，它周围的城镇也靠它维生。

sentences.en: There was a local economy that was based off of the scraps and trash that came off the base.
sentences.zh: 当地的经济正是建立在基地里产生的废料和垃圾的基础之上的。

sentences.en: And there were people from the town who worked on the base as contractors who would commute every day from their homes and line up at the gate early
sentences.zh: 镇上有人作为合同工在基地工作，他们每天从家里通勤，一大早就在大门外排队，

sentences.en: in the morning and then walk on.
sentences.zh: 然后走进去。

sentences.en: And on the base, they would do odd jobs, laundry, maintenance, you name it.
sentences.zh: 在基地里，他们做杂活、洗衣服、搞维护，应有尽有。

sentences.en: And then in 2014, as the base started to shrink, as an American forces and international
sentences.zh: 然后在2014年，随着基地开始缩减，美军和国际

sentences.en: forces began to leave, you know, these contractors were fired, less stuff came off the base, less scrap, less material.
sentences.zh: 部队开始撤离，你知道的，这些合同工被解雇了，从基地流出的东西变少了，废料变少了，材料也变少了。

sentences.en: So by the time that I visited it, you know, last week, it was very much the end of that chapter.
sentences.zh: 所以当我上周去参观时，你知道的，那真可以说是那一章的结束。

sentences.en: So we've just arrived outside the gates of Bagram Airfield.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚抵达巴格拉姆空军基地的大门外。

sentences.en: It's the largest US base still in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是目前国内最大的美军基地。

sentences.en: It's the last base.
sentences.zh: 这是最后一个基地。

sentences.en: We had visited this row of shops, these brick and steel door.
sentences.zh: 我们参观了这排店铺，这些砖墙和钢铁大门。

sentences.en: I guess it's really a shopping mall called the Bagram Shops.
sentences.zh: 我想这其实是一个名叫“巴格拉姆商店”的购物中心。

sentences.en: We're here, there's, you know, lines of shops.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里，你知道的，这里有一排排的店铺。

sentences.en: People are kind of going about their day as if, you know, the Americans are still here.
sentences.zh: 人们照常过着日子，就好像，你知道的，美国人还在一样。

sentences.en: But on the other side of the walls, there's, there's barely anything left.
sentences.zh: 但在高墙的另一边，却几乎什么都没剩下。

sentences.en: So, I mean, looking into these stores, I mean, the best way to describe it is, is you're kind of looking at the cross between a pharmacy and a Humvee trailer.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，看着这些商店，最好的描述就是，你有点像是在看药房和悍马拖车的结合体。

sentences.en: I mean, they have bathing supplies, shampoo.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们有洗浴用品、洗发水。

sentences.en: They have
sentences.zh: 他们有

sentences.en: food and energy drinks, mostly snacks, you know, little desk fans.
sentences.zh: 食物和能量饮料，主要是零食，你知道的，小桌扇。

sentences.en: I mean, just imagine an office and everything in your office as you move out that you don't really want, or you're not going to take home.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下办公室，当你搬走时，办公室里所有你其实并不想要、或者不打算带回家的东西。

sentences.en: What else?
sentences.zh: 还有什么？

sentences.en: Oh, where did you get these little plaques from?
sentences.zh: 哦，这些小牌匾你是从哪弄来的？

sentences.en: That's kind of what a big chunk of this inventory is, on top of the miscellaneous things that just
sentences.zh: 这基本上占了这些库存很大一部分，除此之外还有各种各样

sentences.en: seem really random, whether it's a tourniquet, you know, a tourniquet or a pair of trauma shears.
sentences.zh: 看起来非常随意的杂物，不管是止血带，你知道的，止血带还是一副战术剪刀。

sentences.en: What's a meal?
sentences.zh: 什么是单兵

sentences.en: Ready to eat?
sentences.zh: 野战口粮？

sentences.en: What flavor is it?
sentences.zh: 是什么口味的？

sentences.en: A military backpack, a lone energy drink, what have you.
sentences.zh: 军用背包、孤独的能量饮料，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But like, who is the clientele for everything you're describing?
sentences.zh: 但是，你描述的这一切，其顾客都是些什么人？

sentences.en: Tourniquets, trauma shears, and also energy drinks and snacks.
sentences.zh: 止血带、战术剪刀，还有能量饮料和零食。

sentences.en: Is that U.S.
sentences.zh: 那是美军

sentences.en: soldiers?
sentences.zh: 士兵吗？

sentences.en: Is that local Afghan people?
sentences.zh: 那是当地的阿富汗人吗？

sentences.en: Who are these stores for?
sentences.zh: 这些商店是为谁开的？

sentences.en: It's whoever, you know, maybe people come from Kabul, you know, from nearby towns to buy these
sentences.zh: 管他是谁，你知道的，也许有人从喀布尔来，你知道的，从附近的城镇来买这些

sentences.en: things that you can't really find anywhere else, doctors or local shops or stores or, you know,
sentences.zh: 你在其他地方很难找到的东西，医生、当地的商铺或商店，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: what have you that needs one of these iteMs. It's just kind of this random grab bag of things that
sentences.zh: 诸如此类需要这些物品的人。这就像是一个随机的大杂烩，里面有些东西

sentences.en: maybe you and I wouldn't think you'd ever need, but someone, you know, around the town of Bagram would at some point.
sentences.zh: 也许你和我永远不会觉得需要，但巴格拉姆镇附近的某个人在某个时候可能会需要。

sentences.en: And so what did these shopkeepers say would become of their businesses once Bagram closed, given how reliant they obviously are on the base?
sentences.zh: 那么这些店主怎么说呢？鉴于他们显然对基地如此依赖，一旦巴格拉姆关闭，他们的生意将会如何？

sentences.en: So I walked down this row of shops with another reporter, Fatima Faizi, and we talked to kind of one after another as we came up to the doors and poked our head in.
sentences.zh: 所以我与另一位记者法蒂玛·费齐（Fatima Faizi）一起走过这排店铺，当我们走到门前并把头探进去时，我们一家接一家地进行了交谈。

sentences.en: How's business been?
sentences.zh: 生意怎么样？

sentences.en: One owner said, you know, business is getting worse by the day and that, you know, the Bagram shops are going to have to be closed.
sentences.zh: 一位店主说，你知道的，生意一天比一天差，你知道的，巴格拉姆的商店将不得不关门。

sentences.en: Has business been good lately?
sentences.zh: 最近生意好吗？

sentences.en: Another said, you know, business was fine because more people were coming because the
sentences.zh: 另一个人说，你知道的，生意还不错，因为有更多的人来，因为

sentences.en: Americans were leaving and there was more inventory.
sentences.zh: 美国人要走了，而且有更多的库存。

sentences.en: More stuff come out of the base and more people come out because they know Americans are leaving.
sentences.zh: 更多东西从基地流出来，更多人出来，因为他们知道美国人要走了。

sentences.en: They haven't come here to buy new stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们来这儿可不是为了买新东西。

sentences.en: But, you know, once that goes, he might, he might have to close.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，一旦这些都没了，他可能，他可能不得不关门。

sentences.en: Is he going to leave Bagram or?
sentences.zh: 他要离开巴格拉姆吗，还是？

sentences.en: So maybe I go to Charikar in the center of Peruvan and start a new job.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我会去帕尔旺省中心的恰里卡尔（Charikar）找一份新工作。

sentences.en: And then, you know, one older gentleman who got very hesitant when I took out my phone to record and didn't want to use his name.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，有一位老年人在我掏出手机录音时变得非常犹豫，不想透露自己的名字。

sentences.en: You know, I had asked, he had a piece of body armor in his inventory and he said something along the lines of, I'm not selling this anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我问过，他的库存里有一件防弹衣，他说了类似这样的话：“我再也不卖这个了。

sentences.en: This is for me.
sentences.zh: 这是留给我的。”

sentences.en: I'm paraphrasing it because tomorrow there's going to be a war, right?
sentences.zh: 我在意译，因为明天就要打仗了，对吧？

sentences.en: Just very hesitant and afraid, you know, that the Taliban were getting closer and closer to Bagram and that he was going to have to use these things that were on the base to
sentences.zh: 就是非常犹豫和害怕，你知道的，因为塔利班离巴格拉姆越来越近，他将不得不使用基地里的这些东西来

sentences.en: defend himself and his family.
sentences.zh: 保护自己和家人。

sentences.en: And how he conveyed that was hostile.
sentences.zh: 他表达这一点的方式充满了敌意。

sentences.en: He didn't know that I was American, but he felt like he was talking to someone who kind of represented the base that I had put him in this situation.
sentences.zh: 他不知道我是美国人，但他觉得自己是在和一个代表着把她置于这种境地的基地的人说话。

sentences.en: I think that kind of spoke to most of these shopkeepers that there was just this sense of betrayal, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这某种程度上说明了大多数店主的心声，那就是存在着一种背叛感，对吧？

sentences.en: That the Americans had left this puzzle, this, these 20 years of war without any resolution.
sentences.zh: 美国人留下了这个烂摊子，这20年的战争没有任何结局。

sentences.en: The Taliban still running around the countryside, civilians dying from airstrikes.
sentences.zh: 塔利班仍然在乡间游荡，平民死于空袭。

sentences.en: You know, nothing had really changed in the last 20 years except the Americans were leaving.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在过去的20年里，除了美国人要离开之外，什么都没有真正改变。

sentences.en: That was the feeling, whether that's the reality or not.
sentences.zh: 这就是这种感觉，不管这是否是现实。

sentences.en: And I mean, you could debate that for, for hours, but that was definitely how, how these shopkeepers felt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以就此争论几个小时，但这绝对是这些店主的真实感受。

sentences.en: Is he worried about having to fight the Taliban soon?
sentences.zh: 他担心很快就要跟塔利班作战吗？

sentences.en: Um, yes, we have to, if they can occupy our land, yes, we have to pick up guns and fight it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，我们必须这样做，如果他们占领我们的土地，是的，我们必须拿起武器战斗。

sentences.en: And this is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's this distinct fear of the Taliban returning, you know, they're within
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们对塔利班卷土重来有着一种明显的恐惧，你知道的，他们距离巴格拉姆

sentences.en: 50 miles of Bagram and getting closer as they advance across the north and other parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 只有50英里，而且随着他们在北方和该国其他地区的推进，距离越来越近。

sentences.en: But they're not just afraid of the Taliban, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们害怕的不只是塔利班，对吧？

sentences.en: This idea that keeps getting floated around of another civil war.
sentences.zh: 这种不断被提及的再次爆发内战的想法。

sentences.en: I mean, you could argue that Afghanistan's been in some degree of a civil war for the last
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以争辩说阿富汗在过去的

sentences.en: 40 years.
sentences.zh: 40年里一直在某种程度上处于内战之中。

sentences.en: But as the Taliban get closer and everybody starts picking up weapons, you know, it's impossible to tell who's the good and the bad, who's taking out a local feud on, on someone
sentences.zh: 但随着塔利班越来越近，每个人都开始拿起武器，你知道的，根本无法分清谁好谁坏，谁是在借机了结与某人的

sentences.en: or not, or, or what have you.
sentences.zh: 私人恩怨，还是别的什么。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this idea of, of militias rising up, of being threatened, not just by the Taliban and the government, but maybe by your neighbor is very real.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这种民兵兴起、不仅受到塔利班和政府的威胁、甚至可能受到邻居威胁的想法是非常真实的。

sentences.en: So, well, that makes me wonder, TM, on the ground, where you are in Kabul and where you were around Bagram, how much can you see and feel this rising sense of peril, whether it's
sentences.zh: 这让我不禁想知道，蒂姆，在地面上，在你所在的喀布尔以及你所在的巴格拉姆周边，这种日益增加的危机感有多大程度是可以被看到和感受到的，无论是

sentences.en: in the form of the Taliban approaching, you said they're within 50 miles, or militias picking up arms and the country descending into civil war?
sentences.zh: 以逼近的塔利班的形式——你说他们距离只有50英里，还是民兵拿起武器、国家陷入内战？

sentences.en: How real is all that threat at this moment, given the state of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 鉴于美军撤离的现状，

sentences.en: withdrawal?
sentences.zh: 这一切威胁到底有多真实？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, in Kabul, it's, it's kind of like a bubble, you know, things carry on, as you'd expect.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，在喀布尔，这有点像一个气泡，你知道的，事情照常进行，正如你所料。

sentences.en: I mean, there's this conversation of what comes next.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大家都在讨论接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, that's, that's all around the city on every street corner.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个城市的每个街角都在讨论这个。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But I'd say the indicator that I've encountered that kind of telegraphs that things are getting bad and getting bad quickly was a recent trip to the passport office.
sentences.zh: 不过我想说，我遇到过的一个能预示情况正在恶化且迅速恶化最具代表性的迹象，就是最近去了一趟护照办证处。

sentences.en: You know, these are city blocks that looks like a street festival, as far as the amount of people trying to get passports, families of nine, with people out on the corners with
sentences.zh: 你知道，那里的街区看起来就像一场街头节日一样拥挤，全是争相办理护照的人，有九口之家，还有人在街角摆着

sentences.en: printers trying to talk through, you know, the paperwork needed to fill out the appropriate documents to get a passport to leave, go to Iran, go to Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 打印机，试图帮忙处理填写获取护照所需文件的相关事宜，以便离开并前往伊朗或巴基斯坦。

sentences.en: And there's certainly some level of, of exodus happening.
sentences.zh: 而且确实存在某种程度的离境潮。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, again, it was very apparent down at the passport office.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，再次强调，在护照办证处这表现得非常明显。

sentences.en: So the best evidence that people are terrified is that people are trying to flee the country.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们惊恐万状的最好证据就是大家都在设法逃离这个国家。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm curious how the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道美国

sentences.en: leadership, in particular, President Biden, is talking about this moment, the base closures, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 领导层，尤其是拜登总统，是如何谈论当前局势、基地关闭、美国

sentences.en: leaving, and the terror that it is striking in the hearts and the heads of the people of Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 撤离，以及这些举动在阿富汗人民心中和脑海中激起的恐惧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you know, looking at the April announcement, you know, this, this resolute
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你知道，回顾4月份的宣布，你知道，这，这个坚决的

sentences.en: President Biden saying, you know, we're, we're ending the war in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统说，你知道，我们，我们正在结束阿富汗战争。

sentences.en: You know, this is going to be it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事情就会这样。

sentences.en: We're going to be out by September 11th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在9月11日之前撤离。

sentences.en: And over the last few months, that narrative has kind of changed where he's kind of trying to do two things at once.
sentences.zh: 而在过去几个月里，这种说法已经有所改变，他似乎在同时做两件事。

sentences.en: On one hand, he's trying to convey to the Americans, we're leaving.
sentences.zh: 一方面，他试图向美国人传达：我们要撤了。

sentences.en: And then on the other, to the Afghans, he's saying, well, we're leaving, but we're going to keep supporting you.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他对阿富汗人说：嗯，我们要离开，但我们会继续支持你们。

sentences.en: We're not abandoning you.
sentences.zh: 我们不会抛弃你们。

sentences.en: We're going to keep, you know, giving you money for humanitarian projects, for the security forces.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们会继续为你们的人道主义项目和安全部队提供资金。

sentences.en: We're going to keep 650 troops at the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们将在美国

sentences.en: embassy.
sentences.zh: 大使馆保留650名士兵。

sentences.en: And it's a line that I think is, is impossible to walk, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一条无法走通的路线，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's still going to be that sense of abandonment in Afghanistan because the Taliban are taking broad swaths of the, of the countryside.
sentences.zh: 因为阿富汗仍然会有那种被抛弃的感觉，因为塔利班正在占领大片大片的乡村地区。

sentences.en: So I think in the next couple of weeks or, you know, by September 11th, President Biden will have to find a way to deliver whatever that final message is going to be, that this
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在接下来的几周内，或者说在9月11日之前，拜登总统必须找到一种方法来传达最终的信息，即这场

sentences.en: is over, or we're still going to be here helping the Afghans just without as much troops.
sentences.zh: 战争已经结束，或者我们仍将留在这里帮助阿富汗人，只是没有那么多军队。

sentences.en: I always think back to 2001, to September 11th, and to the reality that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我总是想起2001年，想起9月11日，想起这样一个现实：美国

sentences.en: entered this war in order to try to take out the Taliban, which it believed was harboring Osama bin
sentences.zh: 发动这场战争是为了消灭塔利班，当时美国认为塔利班庇护了奥萨马·本

sentences.en: Laden, who planned September 11th.
sentences.zh: 拉登，而他策划了9月11日袭击事件。

sentences.en: And now, 20 years later, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而现在，20年过去了，美国

sentences.en: is leaving these bases, just as the Taliban is surging towards all these key places and key bases.
sentences.zh: 正在撤出这些基地，而塔利班正气势汹汹地向所有这些关键地点和关键基地推进。

sentences.en: And that always makes me want to understand what that turn of events feels like to somebody who fought in this war, and you have fought in this war.
sentences.zh: 这总是让我想要去了解，对于一个在这场战争中战斗过的人来说，局势发生这种转变是怎样一种感受，而你确实在这场战争中战斗过。

sentences.en: And so I wonder how you kind of make sense of 20 years of fighting to try to take out
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，你如何看待为了试图消灭

sentences.en: the Taliban and then watching the Taliban gaining more and more power at the end of this conflict.
sentences.zh: 塔利班而进行20年的战斗，然后却眼睁睁看着塔利班在这个冲突结束时获得越来越多的权力。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's, that's the ultimate question.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这是终极问题。

sentences.en: That's the, you know, lie in bed at night and stare at the ceiling kind of, kind of question.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种，你知道的，夜里躺在床上盯着天花板思考的问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, you ask maybe the Pentagon, and they'll say, well, we were there to make sure that there were no terror attacks, any more terror attacks on the United States from
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你去问五角大楼的话，他们会说，我们去那里是为了确保不再发生针对美国的恐怖袭击，任何来自

sentences.en: Afghanistan, and we accomplished that mission.
sentences.zh: 阿富汗的恐怖袭击，我们完成了这项使命。

sentences.en: You know, Biden will say, you know, the Americans killed Osama bin Laden in 2011.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拜登会说，美国人在2011年击毙了奥萨马·本·拉登。

sentences.en: So we accomplished the mission.
sentences.zh: 所以我们完成了使命。

sentences.en: But as you said, you know, the initial invasion was to oust the Taliban who had been harboring bin Laden.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，最初的入侵是为了驱逐一直庇护本·拉登的塔利班。

sentences.en: And fast forward all these years, you know, almost two decades.
sentences.zh: 而快进到这些年后的今天，差不多快有二十年了。

sentences.en: And like you said, they're achieving some level of military victory all across the country.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们正在全国各地取得某种程度的军事胜利。

sentences.en: And for someone like me who fought, you know, it's pretty easy to stare up the ceiling and say, hey, we loSt.
sentences.zh: 对于像我这样打过仗的人来说，盯着天花板说‘嘿，我们输了’是件很容易的事。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, that's as bad as far as I can get right now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，目前我能得出的最糟糕的结论也就这样了。

sentences.en: Well, TM, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，TM，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很感激。

sentences.en: Yeah, thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The government of Haiti declared a state of siege on Wednesday after its president,
sentences.zh: 海地政府周三宣布进入戒严状态，此前该国总统

sentences.en: Jovenel Moise, was assassinated by gunmen at his home.
sentences.zh: 若弗内尔·莫伊兹在家中被枪手暗杀。

sentences.en: The president's wife was also hurt in the attack, but is expected to survive.
sentences.zh: 总统夫人也在袭击中受伤，但预计能够幸存。

sentences.en: Four suspects in the attack were killed in a gun battle with police, and two others were arrested.
sentences.zh: 四名袭击嫌疑人在与警察的枪战中被击毙，另有两人被捕。

sentences.en: But their motive remains unknown.
sentences.zh: 但他们的动机仍然未知。

sentences.en: The attack came at a tumultuous moment for both Haiti and Moise, who has clung to power for the past year, even after many had argued that his presidential term had expired.
sentences.zh: 这次袭击发生在海地和莫伊兹动荡不安的时刻，莫伊兹在过去一年里一直紧抓权力不放，尽管许多人认为他的总统任期已经结束。

sentences.en: In a speech, Haiti's interim prime minister condemned the attack and called for calm.
sentences.zh: 海地临时总理在一次演讲中谴责了这起袭击事件，并呼吁保持冷静。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Luke Vanderpluk, Rob Zipko, and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卢克·范德普鲁克、罗布·齐普科和斯特拉·陈制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett, contains original music by Rochelle Bonja and Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由佩奇·考威特剪辑，包含罗谢尔·邦贾和丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为您准备节日期间的待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人在家一样自在的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全黑暗才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会喝断片来助眠。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》App上或您喜欢的任何播客平台上找到《Wirecutter秀》。
